title: Sisyphus: eternal punishment
subtitle: The rock that always falls
subject: mythologie
description: Sisyphus deceives Death, then the gods. His punishment: rolling a rock which falls endlessly. Camus makes it the symbol of lucidity in the face of the absurd.

hero.hook: He cheated Death. The gods give him a rock. And eternity to push it.

blocks.text: **Sisyphus**, legendary founder of Corinth, is the most cunning mortal in Greek myths. His intelligence allows him to challenge the gods. It also earns him the worst punishment: an effort that never succeeds.

In the 20th century, **Albert Camus** transformed this convict into a figure of the human condition. From ancient ruse to modern revolt, Sisyphus asks a simple question: what to do when the goal seems impossible?

says he is the most cunning of men. Sisyphus sees **Zeus**, king of the gods, kidnapping the nymph **Aegina**. Instead of remaining silent, he sells the secret to the girl's father, the river god , in exchange for a water source for his citadel. [[Homer]] [[Asopos]]

Zeus sends **Thanatos**, Death personified. Sisyphus feigns admiration for his chains, asks him for a demonstration... and chains him. Meanwhile, no one dies on Earth anymore. Even the soldiers of **Arès**, god of war, can no longer fall. Ares must free Thanatos by force.
Some linguists compare “Sisyphus” to the Greek *sophos*, “wise”. His name would say “the very wise”: a cruel irony in the face of his fate.

Before dying, Sisyphus orders his wife **Merope** not to give him a funeral. In the Underworld, he complains to **Persephone**, queen of the world of the dead: his wife has dishonored him. He gets three days on Earth to repair. Once in the sun, it refuses to come back.

It is **Hermes**, messenger of the gods and conductor of souls, who brings him back by force to . The punishment is tailor-made: pushing a huge rock to the top of a hill. Each time, just before the goal, the stone comes back down. [[Hades]]
In some ancient traditions, the Rock of Sisyphus explained the tidal cycle or the daily movement of the sun.

Unlike , whose liver is devoured, Sisyphus is not injured in his flesh. Its torture is uselessness. In **1942**, Camus published *The Myth of Sisyphus*. For him, Sisyphus is the : he knows that the rock will fall, and it is precisely this lucidity that makes him grow. [[Prometheus]] [[absurd hero]]
In psychiatry, we have sometimes spoken of “Sisyphism” to describe the repetition of exhausting and useless actions.

Camus defines the  as the clash between our need for meaning and the silence of the world. Each descent of the mountain, Sisyphus resumes his task. His revolt is to continue knowingly. “You have to imagine Sisyphus happy. » [[Absurdity of Camus and Sisyphus]]

The expression “Sisyphean work” refers to a difficult, repetitive and pointless task. In the modern world, the myth speaks to assembly line workers and employees caught in endless procedures. The , wanting to deceive the gods, also becomes a lesson on the limits of trickery. [[The hubris of Sisyphus]]

Yet the story retains one strength: despite the announced failure, the effort continues. The rock falls again, but it does not erase the climb. Sisyphus survives because he embodies resilience in the face of a destiny with no guarantee of victory.
**Sisyphus** deceives Death and the gods, then pushes a rock eternally. **Camus** makes it the symbol of lucidity: knowing the absurd, and continuing anyway.
